video_title: Pirelli CEO: Formula One, Smart Tyres and Europe’s Car Industry | Podcast | In Good Company
gist: Pirelli CEO Andrea Casaluci tells Nicolai Tangen that Pirelli has narrowed to consumer high-value tyres (82% of turnover, near 90% in Europe) to shield itself from Chinese trade-down, uses Formula 1 as a lab for virtual development that cut time to market 30%, sees its data-collecting Cyber Tyre as key to autonomous driving, plans to scale its Rome, Georgia plant from under 500k to 6 million tyres in seven years (US local production is only ~5% of US sales), and calls for a real EU industrial policy for EVs while warning about Chinese speed.

insights.claim: Pirelli now makes only consumer car and motorbike tyres, having exited truck and other large tyres, and 82% of its turnover is high-performance tyres, close to 90% in Europe.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Pirelli's mix is concentrated in the premium segment with better pricing power than mass-market tyre makers.

insights.claim: Casaluci says European tyre manufacturing has lost competitiveness versus five years ago due to imported natural and synthetic rubber, US duties on exports and a huge trade-down to Chinese brands entering Europe.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Margin pressure for mass-market European tyre producers; premium focus is the defensive strategy.
insights.quote: if you manufacture a tire today in Europe, you lost competitiveness compared to five years ago

insights.claim: High-performance tyres are more protected from Chinese and Asian competitors because they lack car makers' trust, quality and performance track record there, keeping competition lower and prices higher - though Chinese performance is improving year after year.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Pirelli's moat depends on staying ahead on innovation; watch Chinese premium tyre progress as a key risk.
insights.quote: The competition is lower the price is higher.

insights.claim: In a materials tender, European suppliers took two months just to return an NDA while a Chinese supplier returned a physical prototype, which Casaluci attributes to lean organizations, no legacy supplier bases and single-person fast decision making.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Chinese supply-chain speed is a structural competitive threat to European industrial suppliers.
insights.quote: The Chinese came back with a physical prototype.

insights.claim: Pirelli's China operations, started 20+ years ago as a cost-efficient manufacturing hub near German car makers, are now an R&D hub serving Chinese premium newcomers who demand low rolling resistance at low temperatures, comfort and very fast time to market.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Pirelli has exposure to the rise of Chinese premium EV brands as an OE supplier.

insights.claim: The US is about 40% of the global high-value tyre market, but only ~5% of Pirelli's US sales are made in the US, ~55% come from its Mexico plant and ~40% are imported from Europe and South America.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Pirelli is heavily exposed to US import tariffs and FX until local capacity ramps.

insights.claim: Pirelli's US market share is below its Asian and European share, and it is investing about $1 billion to scale its Rome, Georgia plant from a bit under 500,000 tyres to 6 million within seven years.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci; Nicolai Tangen
insights.so_what: A multi-year US capacity ramp supports US share gains and reduces tariff exposure.

insights.claim: Casaluci says the US plant decision predated tariffs and is mainly about 360-degree supply-chain resilience against tariffs, FX volatility and logistics costs over a 20-30 year horizon.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Localization is a structural trend for auto suppliers beyond any single tariff regime.

insights.claim: Pirelli has been sole Formula 1 tyre supplier since 2011 and will become sole supplier to MotoGP from next year, and it races in about 350 motorsport competitions annually.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Expanding motorsport exclusivity strengthens premium brand positioning, especially with F1's younger, more gender-balanced audience.

insights.claim: Because F1 tyres must be developed before the car exists and with few physical tests, Pirelli built virtual modeling there and transferred it to road tyres; simulation and AI now cut time to market by 30%.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Faster development cycles help Pirelli match OEM targets and counter Chinese speed.
insights.quote: This is helping us to reduce by 30% the time to market

insights.claim: Pirelli supplies premium brands including Ferrari, Lamborghini, Bentley, Maserati, McLaren, Aston Martin, Porsche and Rolls-Royce, and Casaluci notes 100% of prestige cars are still manufactured in Europe.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Pirelli's OE franchise is tied to European luxury car makers, a segment less exposed to Chinese competition.

insights.claim: EVs raise tyre requirements because they are heavier (higher load index), have stronger torque requiring more grip, and lack engine noise so tyre noise drives comfort.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: EV adoption shifts mix toward higher-spec, higher-value tyres.

insights.claim: Pirelli's Cyber Tyre, developed over about 20 years, collects data on asphalt, driving style and tyre condition and feeds systems like ABS to shorten braking distances; it is already on cars from McLaren, Aston Martin and Pagani.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Tyres becoming a data product could add software-like value to Pirelli.

insights.claim: Casaluci argues that in autonomous driving the brake-versus-steer decision will be fully data driven, making the tyre's real-time grip estimator a key input.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: Positions Pirelli as a sensor/data supplier to autonomy stacks.
insights.quote: The key information to take the right decision, which will be data driven, 100% data driven, is the grip estimator.

insights.claim: Casaluci says Chinese car makers lead premium segments in infotainment, autonomous driving and electric powertrains while being cost competitive, and Europe must accelerate innovation and factory automation, digitization and electrification.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: European OEM competitiveness gap persists; factory automation suppliers could benefit.

insights.claim: Casaluci argues the EU set ambitious Green Deal electrification targets without industrial policy (purchase incentives, charging infrastructure), unlike Norway where 90%+ of new registrations are EVs, and says 'technological neutrality' creates buyer confusion because there is no real alternative to electrification.
insights.speaker: Andrea Casaluci (Pirelli CEO)
insights.so_what: EU policy uncertainty is slowing European EV adoption; watch for incentive or charging policy changes.
insights.quote: Europe just declared the target without helping with an industrial policy.
